A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DSBench. Their text, tables, figures, equations, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching the relocated analyses and extended case studies.

before.justification: v1 reports original model and agent evaluations, human comparisons, and qualitative analyses, including Tables 4, 5, and 7 and the appendix validation of semantic judging.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Tables 4, 6, and 8 and Appendices F and I.

M1.justification: The benchmark task interfaces, semantic answer judging, and baseline input and execution procedures remain unchanged. Simplified descriptions of the toolset do not establish a different algorithm or agent procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use 466 questions from 38 ModelOff challenges and 74 Kaggle modeling competitions. Changing the abstract's source name from Eloquence to ModelOff corrects it to match v1's main text; it does not establish different data coverage.

E2.justification: The model-only, AutoGen, Code Interpreter, and sampled human comparisons retain the same participants. The human row added to v2 Table 4 redisplays the existing 10-competition result from v1 Table 5, whose complete comparison remains in v2 Table 8.

E3.justification: The 80:20 Kaggle split, evaluation metrics, model configurations, and testing procedures are retained. Human comparisons still cover 10 analysis challenges and 22 modeling competitions, and semantic-judge validation still uses 100 answers.

E4.justification: The analyses by challenge, input length, and release year, the error categories, semantic-judge validation, and six extended case studies are retained. Moving qualitative and error analyses to Appendices H and I does not add or remove analytical evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions specify one generated solution per instance; this disclosure moves from v1 Appendix C to v2 Appendix A. Neither version reports repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the benchmark scores.

E6.justification: Matched scores and findings are unchanged. AutoGen with GPT-4o retains 34.12% analysis accuracy; AutoGen with GPT-4 retains 87.84% modeling task success and 45.52 RPG. Sampled human comparisons and appendix outputs also match. Dataset-summary differences are equivalent rounding.

T1.justification: The task formulations and RPG definition are mathematically unchanged; v1 Equation 1 becomes an inline formula in v2 Section 2.2.2. The case-study equations are retained with different numbering, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the same benchmark construction, RPG normalization contribution, realistic task characteristics, and difficulty for existing models and agents. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain their substantive contribution and performance claims.

C2.justification: v1 Section 6 is removed without an equivalent replacement. This removes explicit qualifications about Kaggle-only modeling coverage, missing broader modalities, and the limited baseline approaches. The interpretations of context-length effects, release-year patterns, and observed errors remain.

D1.justification: Model versions and sizes, four-A100 hardware, greedy decoding, prompt templates, Pandas conversion, file-access procedures, and code/data availability are retained. v2 Appendix A consolidates information previously distributed across the experimental section, table caption, and inference appendix.

R1.justification: Section 4 adds BigCodeBench, CodeRAGBench, RepoBench, ML-Bench, and work on hallucination mitigation and visual entailment. These broaden the references without substantially changing DSBench's positioning around whole-system data-science evaluation. The FAITHSCORE publication update concerns an already cited work.

P1.justification: The document is substantially reorganized: experimental details, sampled human comparisons, and qualitative/error analyses are consolidated into reorganized appendices. Task exposition and related work are condensed and rewritten, and descriptive analysis headings are added. The title grammar and abstract's ModelOff attribution are also corrected.

P2.justification: The main-text and appendix layout is substantially revised. Dataset Tables 2 and 3 become side by side; the sampled comparison and two illustrative figures move to appendices; the metric-distribution chart is repeated in Appendix D; and Table 4 redisplays the existing human result. Captions, sizing, and spacing also change.

improvement.justification: v2 improves organization, corrects the ModelOff attribution, and broadens related work. However, it removes v1 Section 6's explicit warning about Kaggle-only coverage and missing broader modalities while retaining broad claims of real-world representativeness. With that coverage unchanged, losing this qualification modestly weakens transparency about generalizability, outweighing the mainly editorial gains.
